item.title: Re: NHS staff survey: Nearly one in six resident doctors physically attacked at work last year
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I was surprised to read the comment in first paragraph of this article given that it is not born out by the results of the survey. The piece correctly reports that ethnic minority doctors are less likely to be subjected to physical violence at work compared to white doctors. item.title: MenB outbreaks: vigilance beyond classical signs
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, This report on the MenB outbreak in Kent appropriately emphasizes rapid treatment and public health response. However, early clinical recognition in young adults may be more challenging than suggested. Initial symptoms of invasive meningococcal disease are often nonspecific and may resemble viral illness, dehydration, or alcohol-related effects—particularly relevant in a nightclub-associated outbreak. item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor When I met Tessa ten years or so ago, she waited not a minute before she began to recruit me to the Patient Panel of the British Medical Journal. She told me that being both a physician and a patient provided us with a unique opportunity to further the common interests of both groups. item.title: Re: Experts outline “urgent” need for more pregnant women to be included in clinical trials
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor. The British Pharmacological Society (BPS) is correct to highlight the lack of evidence of benefits and harms of medication taken by pregnant and breastfeeding women. The problem stems from their routine exclusion from clinical trials, dating from the time of the thalidomide tragedy. item.title: Re: How does covid-19 affect the skin?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, This article is really interesting and thanks for publishing it. Recently we have seen an increased number of scabies cases in the community in the Northeast of England and found it difficult to treat at times, as well as difficult to contain in an outbreak situation. item.title: Re: Assessment and prevention of falls in older people and in people 50 and over at higher risk—summary of updated NICE guidance
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Whilst respecting the thoughtful work gone into this, most of us probably know that much of the guidelines are an ambition rather than a realistic offer to older people who realise themselves that prevention can be better than a fall. The guidelines could usefully include the offer of a hearing test as having ear problems is the cause of many avoidable falls. A simple removal of wax build up can prevent loss of balance. item.title: From Fragmentation to Integration: A Systems-Based Response to the SEND Crisis
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Gilbert’s incisive analysis of the 2026 SEND White Paper critically addresses a system experiencing systemic instability [1].
